en: Advayavajra’s Works 19. *Nirvedhapañcaka*,
edited by Mahāmahopādhyāya Hara Prasad Shastri.
In the *Advayavajrasaṃgraha* (GOS 1927, Baroda),
edited by the Mikkyō Seiten Kenkyūkai, page 4;
in the *Annual Report of the Institute for Comprehensive Studies of Buddhism, Taishō University*.
The world is pure through the awakening of the Buddha, its kinsman.
O Primordially Pure Great Buddha, what is it that is awakened within the teaching of the Buddha?
These are the spontaneous words of one who possesses innate world-weariness and whose conceptualizations regarding the reality of the result and its opposing factors have ceased:
"Knowledge is stainless, empty, effortless, and compassionate in nature;
it arises dependently and is devoid of intrinsic existence. (2)
By this, he describes that which corresponds to the stage of penetration:
"The emptiness of phenomena is wind; compassion is wind;
the power of restraint is wind; and pure conventional reality is wind. (3)
With this, he utters a full outburst of the coemergent (*sahaja*):
"Alas! What shall we say? How shall we say it? Or rather, where indeed are those people?"
For those whose mental activity becomes characterized by effortless spontaneity, [this occurs]. || 4 ||
By this, through his compassion, he makes known the rarity of those persons who possess faith in the profound principle of the Dharma, which is non-abiding and ineffable:
"Indeed, from the seed of my own karma-sūtra, the fruit that cuts to the very marrow has ripened for me;
even though I am a violent man, I have not [inflicted such harm] upon others, for I am thus endowed. (5)
By thus embracing all sentient beings whose minds are afflicted and bound by the thread of their own karma, he reveals the heart of the Bodhisattvas. The *Nirvedhapañcaka* is completed.
Farewell.
